video.title: The Low-to-High Forehand is Mostly a Myth

classification.reason: The coach provides a concrete swing execution instruction for specific situations: when close to the net or when the ball is high, swing basically back to front.

problem.title_as_question: Is the low-to-high forehand swing path mostly a myth?
problem.definition: Players often assume the forehand swing must always be low-to-high, whereas in situations close to the net or on high balls the racket path is predominantly back-to-front with negligible vertical rise.
prerequisites: ball is high or player is close to the net

quotes.text: the low to high forehand is mostly a myth
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: especially when you're close to the net or the ball is high you're swinging basically back to front
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: the elevation gain is so minimal you might not even notice it
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The racket's vertical elevation gain through the swing is minimal or virtually unnoticeable.

causes.statement: When positioned close to the net or dealing with a high ball, the swing moves essentially back to front with minimal elevation gain.

angles.summary: The coach debunks the common dogma that forehands are inherently hit low to high.
The coach explains that situational factors like being close to the net or receiving high balls produce a back-to-front swing trajectory.

solutions.summary: Swing basically back to front when close to the net or when the ball is high.
